positive.original:
I started playing Cyberpunk 2077 expecting a stylish futuristic RPG with a good story and lots of action. And while it definitely delivers on those things, what surprised me the most was how much the game makes you think about your choices.
In many games, decisions feel simple. You usually know which option is the “good” one and which one is the “bad” one. In Cyberpunk 2077 it rarely works like that. A lot of the time you read the dialogue options and honestly don’t know what the best decision is. You sit there thinking about the situation, the characters involved, and what might happen next. Sometimes every option feels risky in its own way.
What makes it even more interesting is that the consequences don’t always show up immediately. You might make a decision and then continue playing for hours before realizing that something later in the story happened because of that earlier choice. When that happens, it really makes you reflect on what you did. There were moments when I spent several minutes just staring at the dialogue options, thinking so much that my head almost started to hurt.
The world itself is also one of the strongest parts of the game. Night City feels alive, full of different districts, characters, and small details that make the environment believable. The atmosphere, the neon lights, the music, and the overall cyberpunk aesthetic make exploring the city really enjoyable. Sometimes just walking or driving around the city can be fun on its own.
The characters are another highlight. Many of them feel well written and realistic, with their own personalities, problems, and motivations. Because of that, the choices you make in conversations feel even more important. You start caring about what happens to these characters, which makes the story much more engaging.
The gameplay itself is also quite flexible. You can approach situations in different ways depending on your playstyle. Some players prefer stealth, others go for direct combat, and the game allows you to experiment with different builds and abilities.
Of course, the game isn’t perfect. Sometimes there can still be small bugs, and a few mechanics could feel a bit more polished. But overall, the experience is still very strong, especially because of the story, the atmosphere, and the meaningful choices.
For me personally, Cyberpunk 2077 is a game that really stands out because it constantly makes you think about your decisions and their consequences. It’s not just about completing missions, it’s about being part of the story and shaping how it unfolds.

[h3] My rating: 10/10 [/h3]

positive.original:
Cyberpunk 2077 with Phantom Liberty isn’t just a game, it’s a first‑person midlife crisis with ray tracing and way too many cool jackets.

Night City is the only place where you can be a broke merc, a glitchy rockstar, and an unlicensed therapist for traumatized NPCs all in the same side quest.
You log in to “do one quick gig” and somehow end up knee‑deep in corpo conspiracies, brain surgery, and philosophical arguments with the voice in your head.

Builds range from anime katana monster to cyber‑wizard hacker to “I put points everywhere and now people just evaporate when I look at them funny.”
Every fight is either a flawless John Wick montage or you screaming, over‑healing, and throwing grenades at your own feet.

Phantom Liberty is basically Season 2 of the story: darker, sharper, and with just the right amount of Idris Elba judging your life choices.
Dogtown feels like a compressed warzone where every quest starts simple and ends with you staring at the screen, wondering if you accidentally picked the bad ending again.

Cyberpunk 2077 now is the game where you boot it up to change your outfit, then realize it’s 3 AM, you’ve finished another ending, and your screenshot folder has doubled in size.

Builds range from anime katana monster to cyber‑wizard hacker to “I put points everywhere and now people just evaporate when I look at them funny.”
Every fight is either a flawless John Wick montage or you screaming, over‑healing, and throwing grenades at your own feet.

Phantom Liberty is basically Season 2 of the story: darker, sharper, and with just the right amount of Idris Elba judging your life choices.
Dogtown feels like a compressed warzone where every quest starts simple and ends with you staring at the screen, wondering if you accidentally picked the bad ending again.

Cyberpunk 2077 now is the game where you boot it up to change your outfit, then realize it’s 3 AM, you’ve finished another ending, and your screenshot folder has doubled in size.

positive.original:
I love this game with every cell of my body. Not just because I love the cyberpunk genre, but because of its story and characters. I always end up coming back to replay it and I never get tired, even knowing everything that happens. This game was there for me during the worst moments of my life and helped me immensely by making me forget my problems, even if only temporarily.
The friendship that V and Johnny form as the story progresses is beautiful to see. A rockstar surrounded by people he considered 'friends' and fans who couldn't even stand to be in the same room as him yet V was there, putting up with his madness and nonsense 24/7, always listening and talking to him like a true friend. V could have taken the pills to get rid of Johnny temporarily at any time but chose to keep him there, which makes their bond feel truly genuine.
The story is obviously one of the highlights. Seeing V go from just a random mercenary wanting the good life in Night City to a person desperate to survive having to help others to try and save themselves. Even if 'helping someone just to save yourself' sounds selfish, V doesn't just save them; they build real bonds.
The gameplay is also super fun, letting you experiment with many different builds. If you want to go 'guns blazing,' you can; if you want to play as a hacker, being a terrifying Netrunner to the NPCs, go right ahead. The game offers a great diversity of builds without forcing you into a single playstyle. The side quests and quests, in general, are also excellent. To me, the best side quests are the ones featuring Johnny’s commentary because it adds an 'extra spice' to them, and the main quests are simply incredible.
The endings are also amazing, especially 'Temperance' and 'The Star.'
SPOILERS***>>**
Personally, the 'Temperance' ending is and always will be my favorite. V sacrificing themselves at the end and going beyond the Blackwall with Alt Cunningham so Johnny can have a second chance at life giving him the opportunity to make different choices is exactly what I feel V would do after everything they went through together. You can clearly see Johnny actively making the most of this second chance. It’s a 'sad' ending, so to speak, but I still find it beautiful: Johnny visiting V’s grave one last time, leaving the bullet necklace, and leaving Night City by bus to finally move on, thanking V for the second chance.
Now, 'The Star' ending features V becoming part of the Aldecaldos nomad family, whom they helped so much during the campaign. When they said they would help V no matter what, they weren't kidding. Raiding Arasaka Tower with the nomads feels like a suicide mission, yet they don't give up, choosing to go to the end with V even if it costs them their lives which is exactly what happens. After the chaos of the raid and returning to their body, V and the Aldecaldos decide to leave Night City to search for a cure. This ending gives a bit more hope that the protagonist might survive after everything, but it's left open-ended. Many consider this the best ending of Cyberpunk 2077, and I don't blame them; it makes total sense to choose it.
Anyway, I'm just rambling about how much I love this game! :P

positive.original:
Night City feels alive now, especially after all the updates. This is the version the game should’ve been at launch, and it’s honestly one of my favorite games at this point.

Edgerunners makes it hit harder. You start noticing things you didn’t care about before, and the city feels more grounded because you already know how things can end.

Playing as V, you begin to notice parallels all around. The cyberware, the gigs, and the fixers are more than just gameplay systems. The combat feels good, builds are actually fun to use, and there’s enough variety to keep things interesting. The characters and side jobs do a lot of the heavy lifting, way more than the main story at times.

If you loved Edgerunners, this game becomes more than just an RPG; it turns into an extension of that emotional experience. If you played the game first, the anime adds a layer of meaning that makes a second playthrough even more impactful.

If you’ve seen Edgerunners, you’ll get more out of it. If not, it’s still an amazing game.

Welcome to Night City. Just don’t expect a happy ending.

Welcome to Night City. Just don’t expect a happy ending.

positive.original:
I think so much discussion at release focused on what a steaming pile of trash this game's code was that it distracted from both the good and the bad. As I finally visit this game with a complete playthrough well over 5 years later, with I suppose a good chunk of the problems fixed, I can weigh in objectively having never played this game at release time.

First, this game is still horrifically buggy. People who say that the problems have been fixed are grading this on a curve versus the original release. Leaving the room where I flatlined the voodoo guy via the blackwall, I would, for example, be frozen in place while crouching and scope focused while stepping on a bit of conduit on the floor. That simple movement is still unsolved in some cases is glaring. I'm not going to go through all the bugs, just that this is still at a point that the problems are completely immersion breaking and required me to redo from saves many times.

Secondly, Keanu Reeves is a horrifically unsuited for his role here. It was a cheap and tawdry way to promote the game to cast him as Johnny. Keanu excels when he can play someone who is completely overcome by awe (The Matrix) or a stoned idiot (Bill and Ted). These are some of my favorite movies. I don't hate him as an actor. But let's face it, he should be typecasted into a very specific kind of role which is not Johnny. Keanu Reeves cannot play an emotionally stagnant revolutionary displaced decades into the future. This role is much too nuanced for him, and his voice bits come off as overread and contrived in the manner of a high school theater production. It's embarrassing. This comes off to me as cheap PR that compromises the work. Which is sad, because there are many characters here that are so well acted and could have created a timeless emotive experience that was beloved as Skyrim, but they are overshadowed by Johnny's piss-poor dialogue reading.

Anyways, the game is good enough. Play it.

positive.original:
The feeling I had while playing this game is very hard to put into words. CD Projekt Red helped me get through one of the toughest periods in my life thanks to Cyberpunk 2077. For once, this game worked like an antidepressant for me. Every difficult day, I couldn’t wait to get home just to play for an hour, to escape harsh reality for a bit. And now I realize that moment has come, I’ve had my break, and I’m ready to return to real life, improving myself the same way I improved V in the game.
It’s honestly sad to realize that just a few more missions remain, and that’s it, the end of the story. But at the same time, each of us will carry that warm feeling in our hearts after finishing the game - the memories of the journey, the conversations with all the characters, especially with Johnny Silverhand, the entire Night City, Badlands and every single corner of this world. It feels like this is something you just can’t forget. And maybe you don’t even need to. I’m sure I’ll come back to this game more than once, but only when life is in a good place. 

Without a doubt, this is the best game project out there right now. It’ll be hard to top this.

Thank you, CDPR. Thank you, V.
Now it’s time to rise in my own life.

And now I realize that moment has come, I’ve had my break, and I’m ready to return to real life, improving myself the same way I improved V in the game.
It’s honestly sad to realize that just a few more missions remain, and that’s it, the end of the story. But at the same time, each of us will carry that warm feeling in our hearts after finishing the game - the memories of the journey, the conversations with all the characters, especially with Johnny Silverhand, the entire Night City, Badlands and every single corner of this world. It feels like this is something you just can’t forget. And maybe you don’t even need to. I’m sure I’ll come back to this game more than once, but only when life is in a good place. 

Without a doubt, this is the best game project out there right now. It’ll be hard to top this.

Thank you, CDPR. Thank you, V.
Now it’s time to rise in my own life.

positive.original:
Cyberpunk 2077

Well let's start with the fact that the game had a rough start but in the end the game turned out to be as good as the developers told us they wanted to make the game.
The story of V is really great with a lot of comedy, action, drama and a lot of moments that do touch our hearts.
The game has a lot of endings and I suggest you try them all, some are really fun.
I do like how you can chose how to start the game, I mean that group to be from.
The game has a lost of story mission and a lot of fun side quests, some are really random like the vending machine that was 'sentient'.
The gigs are really fun to do and I loved every single one of them.
The gameplay of the game is really well done with so many styles to chose from and lots of different upgrade for your style.
You do have a big variety of weapons or you can just kill people with the netrunner build and just make them you know..... So go out there and be a cyberpsycho and kill everyone.

Man do I love my man Johnny, Keanu Reeves really did a amazing job playing him.
Johnny really is a fun character to have around with you as V.



Cyberpunk 2077: Phantom Liberty

The dlc of this game is just incredible, they did such a good job with it.
The expansion of the story really changes some stuff.
The story adds new endings to the story of V and some are really amazing.
They added new ways to upgrade yourself and lots of new weapons to play with.
I recommend you buy the dlc with the game.


With everything said the game still has some bugs here and there but they are not as frequent as the launch of the game. Keep that in mind.

positive.original:
5+ years on from one of the most historically disastrous launches, Cyberpunk 2077 has become an experience that captivates and immerses the player in a world where nothing truly feels impossible. Not only is Night City itself one of the most fun game worlds I've ever explored, but the characters and gameplay possibilities therein give the game a sense of personality that keeps me wanting to come back and uncover every nook and cranny of it. I finished my first playthrough of CP2077 in a week and started a new one almost immediately - that alone should speak to how captivating the world here truly feels. This is not a game you play for only 30 minutes at a time.

The game world is so immersive, in fact, that while fast travel is an option, I'd sooner jump into a car and drive from point A to point B than use a fast travel point. And I can't say the same about a lot of other open-world games I've played.

Anyway, as far as the gameplay is concerned, it's heaps of fun overall. Being on my second playthrough at the time of writing this review, I've only barely scratched the surface as far as the build options at your disposal are concerned, and I'm looking forward to experimenting with many more different builds - I'm especially eager to try out a build that's less focused on direct combat. Now that isn't to say that the combat is bad - quite the opposite, in fact. It's all sorts of satisfying, especially once you settle into a set of perks and cyberware that synergize with your weapon(s) of choice. Prime example: blades + Berserk = *chef's kiss*.

Now the game does still have some intermittent issues - NPCs are proper idiots sometimes, models and textures have trouble loading, the game might crash outright - but in my experience, game-breaking bugs have been very few and far between all things considered. CDPR definitely did their best to improve the game post-launch, and improve it they did. It's arguably the redemption arc of the decade, and they have my utmost respect for it. In the relatively short time I've actually been playing it, CP2077 has already become one of my all-time favorites, and I expect it to be no surprise why that is the case.

Not only is Night City itself one of the most fun game worlds I've ever explored, but the characters and gameplay possibilities therein give the game a sense of personality that keeps me wanting to come back and uncover every nook and cranny of it. I finished my first playthrough of CP2077 in a week and started a new one almost immediately - that alone should speak to how captivating the world here truly feels. This is not a game you play for only 30 minutes at a time.

The game world is so immersive, in fact, that while fast travel is an option, I'd sooner jump into a car and drive from point A to point B than use a fast travel point. And I can't say the same about a lot of other open-world games I've played.

Anyway, as far as the gameplay is concerned, it's heaps of fun overall. Being on my second playthrough at the time of writing this review, I've only barely scratched the surface as far as the build options at your disposal are concerned, and I'm looking forward to experimenting with many more different builds - I'm especially eager to try out a build that's less focused on direct combat. Now that isn't to say that the combat is bad - quite the opposite, in fact. It's all sorts of satisfying, especially once you settle into a set of perks and cyberware that synergize with your weapon(s) of choice. Prime example: blades + Berserk = *chef's kiss*.

Now the game does still have some intermittent issues - NPCs are proper idiots sometimes, models and textures have trouble loading, the game might crash outright - but in my experience, game-breaking bugs have been very few and far between all things considered. CDPR definitely did their best to improve the game post-launch, and improve it they did. It's arguably the redemption arc of the decade, and they have my utmost respect for it. In the relatively short time I've actually been playing it, CP2077 has already become one of my all-time favorites, and I expect it to be no surprise why that is the case.

positive.original:
This is my FIRST game review that I'm currently writing which includes finishing up the game before giving out any critics. This is a Base game review WITHOUT the Phantom Liberty DLC.

What can I say? Is it Worth? A thousand times, Yes! Night City OWNS you, not the other way around.
Prolly one of the best storylines I've ever played compared to the games I've played in other consoles.

6 Years late. SIX D*MN YEARS of missing out perfection. Lots of emotions are invested in the game. The frustrations of making or choosing out hard choices is truly one of the aspects of the game that I truly love. Excited to buy the DLC and see what the expansion is about after reading a lot of positive criticisms about it

Took me 50 hours to complete the story and the side quests. Mind you that these quests are also well written. 

Played ONLY and HEAVILY on my Handheld consoles.
Ran a solid 60 to 70fps on my gpd win 5. 
Slightly struggled on my Steam Deck OLED having 40fps to 50 but definitely playable.

SPOILER:
Through blind playthrough, I chose Johnny over V in the end. NEVER had a single regret, and probably won't hesitate to do it again.

positive.original:
Once again got it as a gift from a good friend, but it was a plan to get it either case as it is an amazing game.
The review will be for both the base game and the Phantom liberty DLC, based on multiple playthroughs and exploring.

First of all I will mention my setup as for this game that is really important and it gives more prospective, processor i7-12700K, 32GB DDR5 @6000 CL30, nvidia 5060 TI 16GB, installed on a nvme drive. The game was run on 1440p with DLSS 4.5 forced with path tracing enabled and frame generation x3 for most runs.

[h3]Positives:[/h3]
[list]
    [*]Well we have to start with the visuals, this game is extremely stunning with the visuals, on the first playthrough you will spend more time looking around than actually playing the game, it really dominates visually, especially with path tracing.
    [*]Attention to detail, you are going to notice it all over the place, especially small details that you would not expect.
    [*]The audio is the next thing that is also up there, and here the top place is for the prime example on how great it comes out when you get great voice actors, not to mention that the ingame radio has awesome songs, and the battle music really fits the whole atmosphere.
    [*]RPG elements are well made and balanced, you do get a bit overpowered but it fits the game lore perfectly.
    [*]Variety of weapons to use and there is something we haven't seen in other games, netrunning abilities, it adds a unique way of playing.
    [*]Map is big, with tons of things to do and explore, with many distinguish spots that look apart from each so you can feel that now you are in the different place.
    [*]A lot of vehicles to traverse the vast map, even though you have fast travel, you can use the auto driver feature to enjoy the scenery.
    [*]Many factions that are different in their looks, talk and way they react to you, each fixed in their own block with some overlaps.
    [*]And do not let me started with how many different unique characters you are going to meet in game, many are complex characters with twists.
    [*]Keanu Reeves - do I need to say more?!
    [*]Idris Elba - not as much bonding on the screen as Johnny, but he filled the role pretty good.
    [*]Story is great, it has all you need, ups, downs, twists, comedy, annoyances, rage, culminations, etc... it is nice that some choices do matter on the story.
    [*]You want to play guns blazing?! No one is stopping you, oh you prefer stealth, go ahead it is optimized for it, netrunning it more your thing?! Well you will be able to make some superb combos. I want to say, you can play any way you like there is no limit and the game is not hindering you if you do not play a meta build.
    [*]The game is extremely well optimized for fast pace movement and slow motion.
    [*]Multiple endings, each one being different and unique in it's nature, and the main thing that was a surprise, as I cannot recall the last game that had this, once you get to the ending you get to play a bit more afterwards to have that proper feeling that you reached the end.
    [*]I feel like this needs to be mentioned, as they are one of the proper good ones, the developers are CD project RED.
    [*]Modding!!! This is done pretty good, with full support on how to get into modding, so if you want to tinker around and learn to code a bit, it can be done, but it is easier to go on Nexus mods, and just download the ones that you like the most, more than 10000 mods available. ps You do need a an account there but it is free and fast to create.
    [*]There is a character creation, it has fairly good options to create unique looks.
    [*]Great option from the developers, you can enable mature filter and it will hide certain scenes and characters will have at least underwear, this is really good as without this you would not be able to stream on youtube for example many parts of the story for example. There is also an option to remove songs from the radio that are copyrighted.
    [*]Optimized for DLSS, FSR, XeSS, choose whichever based on which video card you have, you lose a bit of quality that you will not notice unless you are looking for it hard and in return you will gain a nice boost in fps ( depends from system to system and the ingame settings you are using ).
[/list] 

[h3]Negatives:[/h3]
[list]
    [*]It still has issues, none of these are game breaking in a sense that you cannot fix all of them by either restarting the game or reloading a save game. I did get 2 game crashes as there is still a memory leak issue, happens mostly if you teleport many many times in quick successions and once when I overdid it with forcing the mod to spawn more police. Sometimes your dashing will put you through the floor, sometimes kerenzikov will not work.
    [*]Have to mention this, there is a one big inconsistency with the story that bothers me, without spoiling it, you will figure it out once you replay it.
    [*]Many choices are there as props and have no impact, which is a failure in my opinion, you force me to react but I get nothing no matter what I do.
    [*]As mentioned above, attention to detail is always a double edged sword, if you add some things and then fail to make others that are expected to be working, not work... is jus disappointing.
    [*]Even though there is plenty of weapons to play with, it felt poorly optimized for this masterpiece, simple example once you find the one iconic that fits your play style that is the only thing you will use for, in some cases, 90% of the game. Weapon modding is also simplified, compared to how cyberware was done, this felt like -lets just add this as an option. Prime example - why give me a silencer for an AR or SMG, if you cannot use it as a stealth weapon, to hear it a bit less? To have a cooler sound when you shoot?
    [*]Takedowns could have been done better to add more variety.
    [*]You do get to create your own character, visually I mean, but it felt more of just being there as an option that leads nowhere as you do not get to see yourself at all, except at the endings.
    [*]This is a personal opinion based on very hard difficulty, but it is a bit biased as the playthroughs were consecutive, the fighting becomes boring because you do become too overpowered soon, especially if you explore around, it does fit the lore. I had to give myself additional tasks to make it interesting.
    [*]Some of the mods would be better if they were part of the game to begin with, once you add some of them you do not want to play it without them anymore. This is not a negative per say but more of a notice.
[/list] 

[h1]VERDICT 9/10[/h1]

Definitely a big [b]YES[/b]on this one, and by this one I mean both the main game and the phantom liberty, the DLC is a must, it not only adds to the levels and skills, but enriches the story on it's own, you do get a great storyception there that fits perfectly with the main game.

If you want a futuristic GTA like game with a great story and awesome characters, that lets you play however you like playing without punishing you for it, this is the game for you then. The story is rich and filled with everything you would like to see, if you were watching a movie, but here you play the main protagonist. This might be a spoiler but hopefully not a big one, for me personally, I liked that there is no happy end, that is a such a great curve ball from many other games, and it fits the whole futuristic grim dystopia.

Should you get this game if you cannot run ray tracing or path tracing?
-YES, you should, the game is visually stunning even without those enabled, and yes being able to run either adds more to the visuals, but it is not that you are missing chunks of the game.

If you need videos on how the game worked, looked, how the mods fit, look and work, you can check some of the videos on my profile, be warned for spoilers as they are part of playthroughs.

    [*]Idris Elba - not as much bonding on the screen as Johnny, but he filled the role pretty good.

    [*]There is a character creation, it has fairly good options to create unique looks.
    [*]Great option from the developers, you can enable mature filter and it will hide certain scenes and characters will have at least underwear, this is really good as without this you would not be able to stream on youtube for example many parts of the story for example. [h3]Negatives:[/h3]

    [*]It still has issues, none of these are game breaking in a sense that you cannot fix all of them by either restarting the game or reloading a save game. I did get 2 game crashes as there is still a memory leak issue, happens mostly if you teleport many many times in quick successions and once when I overdid it with forcing the mod to spawn more police.     [*]Have to mention this, there is a one big inconsistency with the story that bothers me, without spoiling it, you will figure it out once you replay it.
    [*]Many choices are there as props and have no impact, which is a failure in my opinion, you force me to react but I get nothing no matter what I do.
    [*]As mentioned above, attention to detail is always a double edged sword, if you add some things and then fail to make others that are expected to be working, not work... is jus disappointing.

    [*]The game is extremely well optimized for fast pace movement and slow motion.
    [*]Multiple endings, each one being different and unique in it's nature, and the main thing that was a surprise, as I cannot recall the last game that had this, once you get to the ending you get to play a bit more afterwards to have that proper feeling that you reached the end.
    [*]I feel like this needs to be mentioned, as they are one of the proper good ones, the developers are CD project RED.
    [*]Modding!!! This is done pretty good, with full support on how to get into modding, so if you want to tinker around and learn to code a bit, it can be done, but it is easier to go on Nexus mods, and just download the ones that you like the most, more than 10000 mods available. ps You do need a an account there but it is free and fast to create.
    [*]There is a character creation, it has fairly good options to create unique looks.
    [*]Great option from the developers, you can enable mature filter and it will hide certain scenes and characters will have at least underwear, this is really good as without this you would not be able to stream on youtube for example many parts of the story for example. There is also an option to remove songs from the radio that are copyrighted.
    [*]Optimized for DLSS, FSR, XeSS, choose whichever based on which video card you have, you lose a bit of quality that you will not notice unless you are looking for it hard and in return you will gain a nice boost in fps ( depends from system to system and the ingame settings you are using ).
[/list] 

[h3]Negatives:[/h3]
[list]
    [*]It still has issues, none of these are game breaking in a sense that you cannot fix all of them by either restarting the game or reloading a save game. I did get 2 game crashes as there is still a memory leak issue, happens mostly if you teleport many many times in quick successions and once when I overdid it with forcing the mod to spawn more police. Sometimes your dashing will put you through the floor, sometimes kerenzikov will not work.
    [*]Have to mention this, there is a one big inconsistency with the story that bothers me, without spoiling it, you will figure it out once you replay it.
    [*]Many choices are there as props and have no impact, which is a failure in my opinion, you force me to react but I get nothing no matter what I do.
    [*]As mentioned above, attention to detail is always a double edged sword, if you add some things and then fail to make others that are expected to be working, not work... is jus disappointing.
    [*]Even though there is plenty of weapons to play with, it felt poorly optimized for this masterpiece, simple example once you find the one iconic that fits your play style that is the only thing you will use for, in some cases, 90% of the game. Weapon modding is also simplified, compared to how cyberware was done, this felt like -lets just add this as an option. Prime example - why give me a silencer for an AR or SMG, if you cannot use it as a stealth weapon, to hear it a bit less? To have a cooler sound when you shoot?
    [*]Takedowns could have been done better to add more variety.
    [*]You do get to create your own character, visually I mean, but it felt more of just being there as an option that leads nowhere as you do not get to see yourself at all, except at the endings.
    [*]This is a personal opinion based on very hard difficulty, but it is a bit biased as the playthroughs were consecutive, the fighting becomes boring because you do become too overpowered soon, especially if you explore around, it does fit the lore. I had to give myself additional tasks to make it interesting.
    [*]Some of the mods would be better if they were part of the game to begin with, once you add some of them you do not want to play it without them anymore. This is not a negative per say but more of a notice.
[/list] 

[h1]VERDICT 9/10[/h1]

Definitely a big [b]YES[/b]on this one, and by this one I mean both the main game and the phantom liberty, the DLC is a must, it not only adds to the levels and skills, but enriches the story on it's own, you do get a great storyception there that fits perfectly with the main game.

This might be a spoiler but hopefully not a big one, for me personally, I liked that there is no happy end, that is a such a great curve ball from many other games, and it fits the whole futuristic grim dystopia.

Should you get this game if you cannot run ray tracing or path tracing?
-YES, you should, the game is visually stunning even without those enabled, and yes being able to run either adds more to the visuals, but it is not that you are missing chunks of the game.

If you need videos on how the game worked, looked, how the mods fit, look and work, you can check some of the videos on my profile, be warned for spoilers as they are part of playthroughs.

positive.original:
When Cyberpunk released years ago, I refunded it (via CDPR's own launcher) after 40+ hours of gameplay because of the game's poor performance. Years later, I decided to dive back into Night City (Cyberpunk + Phantom Liberty) because they "fixed" the game so I got to enjoy the newly patched features like photo mode, new cars, new quests, improved performance etc.. I guess I got to experience the game at its best.

This is one of the best games I have ever played. Tons of possible builds that makes the combat fun, and I personally thought the story (base game and DLC) is well written. I enjoyed most of the quests, specifically the ones that expounds the story of your companions and how it blends into the main story. Night City is beautiful especially with Path Tracing and Ray Reconstruction.

I am aware of the multiple endings already. I am actually just a couple of quests away from finishing the game, but I am holding off because I do not want it to be over lol.

I love this community, and spent a lot of time really backing it and supporting a lot of people who couldn't afford the game.  Even after my giveaway I still bought friends a copy to new viewers in random draws.  This game started rough, but because of a great developer who listened to their fan base made a quite flop into a triple gainer with a corkscrew 180 landing with no splash.  I'm glad to see Asmon and others also championing this game.  It wasn't brilliant but became brilliant.  It's my favorite game ever and will always go to bat for Cyberpunk2077! <3

positive.original:
I originally bought Cyberpunk 2077 on my PS4 on the day it launched. Despite the crashes and performance issues that plagued the game back then, I absolutely loved it. 

I fell in love with Night City, with V, with that bastard Johnny, and with the entire story. It made me smile, laugh, get angry… and even cry. It’s probably the title that has hit me the hardest emotionally.

What I truly appreciate about this game is its incredible environment, gameplay freedom and aesthetic. For me the story is one of the best ever written. The gunplay feels amazing, and the character progression system is incredibly satisfying and stylish.

I bought it on Steam just to dive back into the City of Dreams once again with better graphics. No regrets. I am a fan of developers’ love for that title. They turned it into a top tier masterpiece.

“I just want the world to know I was here, that I mattered.”

positive.original:
Having played through this game at least 6 times, I'd say I've seen what this game has to offer, and it is good. For a game that really screwed up it's launch, it has come a long way, especially after Cyberpunk 2.0 and Phantom Liberty. While it may have had a rough start, even under all the bugs and performance issues, there was still a great game under the grime. Not every game can say the same.

This is a great open world game with some really fun quests, and great gameplay. The gameplay was good but flawed before 2.0, but after the 2.0 update, the gameplay has been refined into a fine wine. It is fun being a cyber ninja chopping everyone in sight to pieces, being a netrunner wizard melting the brains of everyone on the battlefield with but a glance, Or being an assassin blowing the brains out of everyone you come across. The RPG mechanics backing up your playstyle are amazing, and the cyberware is awesome. You can become the ultimate killing machine and it is sublime. 

Story wise, the main quest in this game is amazing, like honestly, the story of V while a tragic one, is a great one. I've seen every ending, and they are all really cool to reach. The "companion" characters and the other major side content are also really great. In the base game, the gigs from fixers are okay, a lot of them are pretty basic shooting galleries. But in Phantom Liberty, the gigs are amazing, they have full stories with interesting characters and interesting and hard choices to make. But also exploring night city is just a blast. There might be a fast travel system, but honestly I almost never use it because driving around night city, dodging traffic at 150mph is super fun, especially with the fine tuning they have done to vehicles, also there are a stupid amount of awesome looking cars, and while you can buy cars, you get plenty of cool ones doing side quests too for free.

My two main complaints for this game are. My first major gripe is that the life paths are very underwhelming, especially in the base game, aside from one extra quest and some special lines of dialog here and there, it really doesn't matter. In fairness, CDPR recognized that as a flaw, and in Phantom Liberty you do actually get a few special options based on what lifepath you have in quests.

My second main complaint is the lack of interactivity and simulation of interactions with the gangs, or more specifically reputation systems with the various factions. Except for a few specific circumstances, your actions don't really have an effect on the gangs of night city, even though you've mowed down hundreds, if not thousands, of them by the end of the game. I would say that expands to more world interactivity in general, and life sim elements that I wish the game had more of, or deeper interactions. There are a handful of mods that move to address this, but they can only go so far without new voice lines, especially for example, romance interactions with the 4 companion characters. So for the sequel, I hope CDPR adds a lot more world interactivity, and life sim elements. Not to the point of say survival, but just to help you feel really immersed in the world. In other words, I want more stuff in the game that isn't just "go and kill everyone here". I suppose it made sense for V as a mercenary, but still.

translations.schinese:
Having played through this game at least 6 times, I'd say I've seen what this game has to offer, and it is good. For a game that really screwed up it's launch, it has come a long way, especially after Cyberpunk 2.0 and Phantom Liberty. While it may have had a rough start, even under all the bugs and performance issues, there was still a great game under the grime. Not every game can say the same.

This is a great open world game with some really fun quests, and great gameplay. The gameplay was good but flawed before 2.0, but after the 2.0 update, the gameplay has been refined into a fine wine. It is fun being a cyber ninja chopping everyone in sight to pieces, being a netrunner wizard melting the brains of everyone on the battlefield with but a glance, Or being an assassin blowing the brains out of everyone you come across. The RPG mechanics backing up your playstyle are amazing, and the cyberware is awesome. You can become the ultimate killing machine and it is sublime. 

Story wise, the main quest in this game is amazing, like honestly, the story of V while a tragic one, is a great one. I've seen every ending, and they are all really cool to reach. The "companion" characters and the other major side content are also really great. In the base game, the gigs from fixers are okay, a lot of them are pretty basic shooting galleries. But in Phantom Liberty, the gigs are amazing, they have full stories with interesting characters and interesting and hard choices to make. But also exploring night city is just a blast. positive.original:
My first review is going on my very first favorite game.  

I love this game, I find it very enjoyable without mods.

There's so many different style of gameplays that you can do within accomplishing anything on Cyberpunk 2077.

I've played numerous 'types' of V. 
Dating all the way back with the funny bugs. 

The storyline is the most captivating part of this game. I implore those to really understand the depth and detail, the thought perceptions and the perspective of V. We're given three options in what lifestyle to choose, and each one carries its own significance. So many different outcomes and many different responses, easter eggs, hidden features, very awesome abilities and utilities. 

This game has a very big meaning, not just that but a recognition in how you make yourself to be in the life of V.
It's very funny to bring out a defining detail from a game to bring out to reality too, there's a big crucial detail of when encountering a monk that only V could see just for the players to do some meditating! That's absolutely amazing.
There are many, many, many, with plenty more detailed scenery and plots with more in-game depth characterized featured storylines and many different ways in approaching them with many different playthroughs. 

I seriously am in love with this game. I'd want to explain it in much more details but just cutting things short that this game has been awesome for me.  


Much love Chooms.

positive.original: This game is something like Grand Theft Auto meets Fallout, and in all the best ways. It's also it's own unique beast, with takes on the RPG genre that blend several different approaches to leveling and advancement in skills. Having played through the original and now the Phantom Liberty DLC, I can definitely say that the game is better now than it ever has been, and was a blast from start to finish. Excellent writing and character development accompany a storyline where your choices matter down the road, sometimes even in very subtle ways. The variety of weapons and hacks and cyberware let you put together some pretty wild builds to pull off all kinds of different play styles as well. Cyberpunk 2077 is absolutely one of my favorite games of all time.

This is the best game ever made, the base games story is good, the graphics are good, Night City is the best open world. But the DLC story is another lvl. 

The driving physics is mid but it never advertised itself as a racing game, and the human NPC AI is disappointing if compared to older games, even Assassin's Creed Unity...

And the RPG elements aren't that good either (exception the DLC)

But its still my favorite video game.

positive.original:
Although I pre-ordered the game, I didn’t actually play it until about a year after release, after a decent patch. It turned out to be one of those games that completely pulls you in, leaving you with that empty feeling when it’s over and wishing it hadn’t ended.

Then Phantom Liberty was released. For me, it was the perfect opportunity to return to Night City and experience it all over again.. and it was worth every cent. I loved every character, the story, the side missions, and the ending.

This is what happens when devs are given the time and budget they need. I’m already very thankful for The Witcher, and now Cyberpunk as well. Thank you for the experience, CDPR.

positive.original: I just picked this up on sale recently complete with the DLC. I never played it when it came out due to reported issues with bugs and crashing.  However, I think it runs fairly well for the size it it, which is massive.  I think the cross-console save setting was causing some crashes for me.  I turned it off and Dogtown (DLC) ran much more consistently.  Mostly, it would crash when I went too fast in game hopping from one point to the other, observably when it auto-saves.  I have only done the side-quests and side-main quests so far. Level 60 since Hour 120, 200+ hours when writing this, and I am finishing up some of the last quests for the side quests.  I have most of the cars, the legendary gear I want, and my cyberware is maxed out to the perk build I went heavy in.  I am amazed at this game's RPG element being so customizable, but I hit the limit/end game with just doing side quests.  Everyone reading this must have already played it before I did. The music is amazing and original, yet familiar.  I started on keyboard, but I switched to controller and like it better.  I mapped a couple of macros for button combinations and I don't think I am missing out with the controller (8bitdo Pro 3). One of my favorites of all time, and I haven't started the main quest yet!  XD

positive.original:
The bad reputation caused by its launch kept me away from this game, until I got invited to a Cyberpunk RED campaign, got wrapped in the wonderfully magnificent pile of lore and beautifully developed setting. Turns out the game wasn't only good and bloody entertaining, but it ended up being one of my favourite gaming experiences in recent years.
The game is lovingly crafted and intriguing all the way to the bitter end, and I was all for it all the way. 
However, Cyberpunk 2077 is far from being a perfect game. There's some writing decisions I felt were pretty weird, the main story is very short, and I found a decent quantity of bugs during my playthrough (nothing game-breaking, though). 
I still believe the game is highly worth it if you are into RPGs, shooters, cyberpunk media or all of the above.

positive.original: Its come a long way from its rough launch but now its near perfect. Really mod friendly. Running this game with 100+ mods and path tracing is a different gravy. Shame it lacks a proper native third person mode because the character customisation is 10/10 and is wasted being locked to first person only throughout majority of the game. However photo mode with mods to unlock extra features and installing pose packs is just brilliant to really show off your character.

positive.original: I'm just a millenial mom over here but I've been playing video games since Oregon Trail. All platforms, all genres, all my life. This is, without question, the best video game I have ever experienced. I've never played anything so immersive and expansive. Reality falls away when you play - suddenly three hours have passed and I feel like I just sat down. I'm still on my first playthrough and I don't want it to end. I love the characters, the night life, the gameplay, the story, the tension. I feel like I'm living in a movie. The dynamic between Johnny and V is so entertaining and...endearing? I get that I'm five years late to the party but I don't think this game will ever fade away. Let me also say that the only other game I've ever sunk into like this is Animal Crossing. Yeah. This game is that good. It will get you, no matter what kind of gamer you are. And no other video game will ever be the same.

positive.original: One of the best AAA games ever made and I mean that genuinely, the characters and storytelling is kinda one of a kind in this game. There is hundreds of hours of little details, missions and collectibles to do literally whatever you want and by jove its just so fun!! The first two parts blew my mind with how much bigger the world became and how busted V becomes. This is weverything i could've asked for as a massive GTA fan when i was a young buck, with both sandevistan and netrunning builds being just ridiculously fun in this huge, infinitely precise sandbox. 9/10 heartwrenchingly sad most of the time tho, perfect vibe, perfect name

positive.original:
Cyberpunk 2077 is an absolute masterpiece in terms of story, world-building, and visual detail. Even years after release, the world feels alive and immersive, and the level of freedom in gameplay is incredible. Driving through Night City on high settings, especially on Ultrawide, is breathtaking—the lighting, reflections, and city details are unmatched.
Performance has improved a lot since launch. With Ultra settings and DLSS, I get smooth gameplay with high framerates. The game also runs perfectly on co-op mods and side activities. The missions are varied, and the choices feel meaningful, which keeps me coming back for more.
Despite its rocky launch, CD Projekt Red delivered an experience that is truly next-level. If you love open-world games with deep storylines, Cyberpunk 2077 is a must-play.
Rating: 10/10 ✅

positive.original:
I've been hooked to Cyberpunk for the few months. I've Completed all gigs, NCPD missions, most of the missions (I'm up 255) completed all the endings... and wow, I've got the urge to start another playthrough!

I'm a 40+ year old gamer who has been playing for decades, there is something very special about this game. The story touches you in places which I've not felt from other games for years. 

The attention to detail in night city is incredible, like others have said the City feels alive. The small details really make a difference, you can really feel the love and passion poured into this game. 

The Phantom Liberty DLC is probably the best DLC out there and should be a game developers master class.

Incredible.

positive.original:
Bought this game expecting I wouldn’t like the first-person view…
Stayed because the immersion is THAT good.

Night City pulls you in like no other game. You go in to do one quick mission and suddenly it’s 3 wait no 4am, you have new cyberware, five side quests, emotional damage, and somehow another jacket you don’t need but had to buy. The world feels alive, the characters actually make you care, and the combat lets you play however you want stealth hacker, katana psycho, or shotgun gorilla with chrome arms.

Story? Hits hard.
Graphics? Welcome to cyberpunk.
Game? Straight till 4am.

If you avoided this game because of the launch… yeah, same. (actually i was broke)
If you try it now, you might accidentally disappear from real life for a week.

10/10 would install cyberware again.
20/10 would choose Panam again. (she rejected me)

positive.original:
Recommended

I only really started playing seriously after the 2.0 update, and the game feels fantastic in its current state.

The graphics are outstanding and Night City is one of the most impressive environments I’ve seen in an RPG. The progression system, combat mechanics, and overall build variety are excellent. You can approach fights in many different ways and experimenting with builds is genuinely fun. In that sense, it’s easily one of the reference titles in the modern RPG scene.

My only small criticism is that the game can be a bit heavy on dialogue at times. Some players will love that level of narrative depth, but personally I found a few sections a bit too talkative. Fortunately, most of it can be skipped if you prefer to keep the pace up.

Overall, after 2.0, Cyberpunk 2077 is an outstanding RPG and absolutely worth playing.

positive.original:
--- Personal Thoughts ---

An incredibly enjoyable open-world RPG looter-shooter experience; The base game provides a palpable power fantasy, and does so by making it exceedingly easy to create an extremely powerful character from messing around with the build & cyberware system. As such, don't expect a challenge. Even on some of the harder difficulties, I wager most people will be able to get through the game with relative ease. By far the strongest part of the game is the environment & story itself. Night City is a vivid, striking cyberpunk dystopia riddled with bright neon literally everywhere. 

The constant firefights happening as you drive through the city, the various gigs you can get, even the random calls you can get from important NPC's that start entire questlines helps sell that this is a city where things are actively moving and happening. The only real criticism with regards to that is a certain time-limited aspect of the narrative that clashes with what is, ostensibly, an unlimited amount of time to engage in the endless amount of side quests throughout the game. 

--- Additional Thoughts on Phantom Liberty ---

Easily one of the most impressive DLC's for a game I've seen so far. It's a step up in terms of voice acting, difficulty balancing, and narrative. The DLC area is incredibly interesting, the characters are complex and compelling, and there are some scenarios in the game that genuinely had my adrenaline pumping. It was never truly unforgiving, but the step up in overall difficulty definitely helped sell a lot of the narrative beats within the DLC (something that the main game, unfortunately, suffers a little from). 

--- Overall Thoughts on the Game ---

*Very* good game. I'd probably put it as it exists right now at around an 8.5/10. Highly recommended if you're into looter shooters with RPG mechanics. Good story and strong environment design. Pick up the main game and DLC if you can afford it, and *definitely* pick it up on a good sale.

positive.original: I was hyped for this game since 2009 when I saw the first trailer for this game. I remember it was such a beautiful trailer and I reflect now on how I used to think, "yeah, it looks good now, but when they release it, the graphics and the game play are going to not be nearly what was reflected in the trailer. Years later, when it finally released, the graphics looked good, but just bugged out all the time. I can now gladly say that with all of the updates and patches from the developers, it is EXACTLY what I hoped it would be years after that first trailer release as well as one of my all time favorite GOATS.

positive.original: It's been a while since I've written. So, I finished Cyberpunk 2077. I finished it three years ago. To my surprise, the game has improved: fewer bugs, more side quests, an improved open world, more character lore, a slightly changed plot, and the Phantom Liberty DLC. Honestly, the DLC, which was about something completely different, was a bit overdone. Spy missions, saving the president, saving Songbird. But most importantly, Reed's character was awesome, making him really cool. With Johnny and Reed's charisma, the game is absolutely fantastic. There are now more endings. What can I say, the game is a masterpiece.

positive.original:
One of the best narrative games of all time.

Story-wise, the game is exceptional with a plethora of choices that impact how the story turns out.

The gameplay in the first-person scenes, I doubt there is a single game on this level.

Customization: sure, a skill tree and cybernetic implants. You wanna smash people with your bare hands, fry their brains, or just blast through them with rockets?

The aesthetic of the game is unique; rarely do we get sci-fi / cyberpunk games like this, and it's really refreshing in a sea of fantasy RPGs.

9.5/10, fully chromed out, choom.

positive.original:
The Redemption of Night City (With Cavéats)
I’ve been here since the beginning, and while Cyberpunk 2077 will be studied as a remarkable turnaround, we shouldn't forget that it launched two years too early. CD Projekt Red arguably got a "free pass" for a state they knew wasn't ready, but the current version of the game is finally something remarkable.

The Good
The World: Night City is visually outstanding. It is easily one of the most detailed environments ever put in a game, and it’s easy to get lost in the atmosphere.

Build Variety: Spec-ing your character is a total joy. The game truly allows you to play how you want, making it incredibly approachable regardless of your preferred playstyle.

Masterful Side Quests: Some of the darker, gloomier side stories are the best parts of the game. They are masterfully written and stand as great stories in their own right.

Combat: Whether you're hacking or shooting, the combat loop is genuinely fun.

The Bad
The Writing: While the characters are mostly great, the dialogue can often be "cringe." V feels somewhat bland as a protagonist, and the character creation system still feels like it lacks meaningful impact.

Navigation: As beautiful as the map is, it just isn’t fun to navigate. Its scale is impressive, but getting from point A to point B often feels like a chore.

The "Arasaka" Irony: There is a lot of deserved love for the game now, but let's not forget the corporate decisions behind the launch. In the end, CDPR acted a lot like the megacorps they satirize.

Verdict
It’s not a solid 5/5, but the story and the sheer detail of the world keep me coming back. It is a must-play for the atmosphere alone, even if the "soul" of the protagonist and the dialogue occasionally miss the mark

My experience is with Steam Deck.
The game looks awesome and runs very smoothly. As a 1st person action shooter, it is ok. As an rpg, it is ok. As a Cyberpunk game, it is great. As a entertainment experience, the game is great, offering lots to do, most of which is exciting. It would be nice if they would not force the "open world" stupidity, such as having to waste the players time whenever they want to do shopping or adjust the cyberware. But with vehicles and fast travelling, it is kept at a tolerable level.

As a entertainment experience, the game is great, offering lots to do, most of which is exciting. It would be nice if they would not force the "open world" stupidity, such as having to waste the players time whenever they want to do shopping or adjust the cyberware. But with vehicles and fast travelling, it is kept at a tolerable level.

positive.original:
I have roughly 80~ hours on this game, coming from PS4 before moving everything over to PC. There are only a handful of bugs, but compared to 1.8.3 to current? It's so, so much better. 

The gameplay is much smoother and runs so much better. But that's not what I want to talk about.

When I first started playing this game a couple months ago, my first impression, upon completing the game, was that it lacked in the story. Going in, I was expecting anti-consumerism and anti-capitalism/corporation themes, and they are indeed there, but not the fore front. I finished the game, complained about it to my girlfriend, then came back and played a few more times, getting a few more endings.

That's when I realized what the game is also trying to point out. Yeah, yeah, consumerism narrative or whatever, but I don't mean that, I mean V, your player.

Post prologue, V has everything ripped from them. Closest friend, they had trust taken and broken, they died and came back and now are stuck with a rockerboy terrorist in their head that's trying to take over their body.

The game has an artificial timer for this, but this is important to mention, the gameplay not forcing this timer is probably the most important to me. As you go through Night City, completing jobs, finding friends, partners, even developing your relations with Johnny, it all sets in, "you're on borrowed time, how will you spend it?"

One ending, which I can barely consider it an ending as it is very abrupt (with the player's choice), you see everyone you met, rubbed shoulders with or were acquainted. Depending on the romance option you chose, they could be furious or broken. Friends torn inside, wishing things were different. 

Another ending, just, give in. Let the corporation win and what becomes of you? You abondoned everything you loved and had. In a sense, betrayal.

This is coming from a girl who came out of a really bad drug addiction and is just getting out of frequent suicide ideation. On surface level, this game asks, "what makes you human," but digging deeper, paying attention to your playthrough, you're asked, "if you're on limited time, you die next week, what do you do? Do you pretend things are fine? Prolong your life at the expense of others and the experiences around you, or do you leave everything behind, abandon it all; leaving behind scars, damaging the people you built community with?"

This game has many problems but its story isn't one of them. This game made me change my perception of what life is. From being nihilistic, hateful, I turned the spotlight and, sure some things didn't change but, my approach to life changed. There are a lot of things I could glaze this game for, a lot of themes I could beg and beg to become a reality. But the change that did happen, within me, I accept. This is a really, really great game. 20-50 hours per save gives you everything you need to experience this game in all aspects and I could not recommend it enough.

positive.original: I’ve been saving Cyberpunk 2077 for a long time, waiting for the right moment when the game had fully matured. I’m incredibly glad I waited. Diving in today, I am genuinely impressed by how elegantly it has aged and how optimally it runs. positive.original:
Okay, hear me out. I've got 160 hours in Cyberpunk that i bought on EGS. Had troubles with several final achievements (they just bugged on me), so i was hoping for the longest time that i can get my platinum on Steam. And few years later — here we are. Bought the game second time as a huge thank you, to the CDPR team.

So listen, Cyberpunk 2077 is a wonderful game. Definitely my favourite CD Project Red game (sorry, Witcher 3 fans). And Phantom Liberty is without a doubt the best DLC to any game i have ever played. Night City is incredibly immersive. Driving through the city in a taxi, looking at raindrops running down the window... Man... This game is just something else.

Maybe i am biased, as i love sci-fi more than fantasy settings in general. But now that the game has been polished. I emplore you — give it a try. The story is great, graphics are still a benchmark, music is cool as hell (check out the OST on any streaming platform), gameplay is greatly improved since version 2.0. And the first person view makes V's journey so much vivid and real.

Cyberpunk 2077 is a cinematic masterpiece that i feel like everyone who loves games has to try at some point. Se ya in the Night City, choom!

negative.original:
This is a tough one to rate. Trying this 5 years after release, with hardware that allows me to experience it in path traced glory on a 4K OLED monitor, I did initially enjoy the novelty of looking at those neons at night and the way light bounces off of of high resolution skin textures. 

However, the game makes me feel awfully empty, and the world while big, is barren, with very little that can be done in it that isn't a subset of repetitive actions. Combined with the dystopian setting, and the game being pretty big, playing it feels.. lonely for the lack of a better term. 

I'm a sucker for large open world games and great graphics, so on paper this was supposed to be a win. But I find myself just not enjoying playing with it, not enjoying interacting with the world in its extremely limited capacity, or the few unique characters that last beyond specific missions.

Despite 5 years passing since launch, I still fell through the ground for the game to crash hours into my playthrough. Despite those same 5 years passing, and there being some more cars, weapons, it feels like the content added is fairly mundate, adding inconsequential type of novelty. I was able to make the world a bit more interesting with mods, as 5 years allowed the community to produce quite a bit. And while the most ambitious can add some things to do, they can't address the fundamental issue of how uninterractable and barren the world feels. 

The negative rating isn't a reflection of the bugs or technical prowess of the developers, which they have demonstrated. The game looks good and generally plays at a C+ reliability level. Totally acceptable if the game was actually fun. But most of it is doing the same few things slightly differently dozens of times. The big city serves little purpose beyond providing a distance you need to drive between places where you do those things. Interesting things happen just during finite missions, and then they end, and the world is unexciting again. If something happens, it's usually a one-time scripted event where you just watch it. There is a whole lot of filler to make the city appear like a city-ish, but you can't do anything with it.
And it leads to an experience that isn't particularly fun, and it isn't as enjoyable as the other large open world games that either add interactivity, or at least introduce pleasant worlds to make up for it. I don't hate this game - I felt indifferent and slightly more negative with each hour spent in the game feeling like more and more of a waste of time on something that didn't feel fun, and I will likely not complete the story, as it feels like too much commitment to something that surprisingly doesn't spark joy.

RedLauncher.exe crashes every 5-20 minutes which crashes Cyberpunk. It's not my PC which I discovered after about 6 hours of troubleshooting and reinstalling drivers, testing RAM, and my GPU. Honestly, I don't know why developers are so hellbent on launchers, I don't know a single person who says "You know what would make this game better? A buggy launcher that crashes the GPU intermittently!" 

Before anyone asks, No I'm not using mods, yes, I've performed a clean install. Yes, everything is up to date.  Yes, other GPU intensive games work.

My only saving grace with this game is that it works on Steamdeck. (Even though its a bit ugly) 

That said- If ANYONE has a fix for this. I would love to give it another go.

negative.original:
Good story hidden behind atrocious jank

Honestly, after finally trying the game, I have no fathomable explanation why it has reviews this positive. It's been years of patches and as a newcomer this is still a buggy, janky mess. Some examples:
- Driving collision is an absolute mess. Sometimes you can't even start the vehicle properly when driving uphill (how can this even happen????)
- Bunch of random crashes, perfectly replicable as well
- Why do enemies forget they were mid-convo with someone when you grab them from behind?
- Why do NPCs drive their cars so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ awfully. Why do they ignore all traffic as if they were just using pre-determined paths

But honestly none of that bothers me as much as seeing that the world is insanely artificial. It's mostly acceptable if you never go off the beaten path but since you are often encouraged to do so... you can see how fake everything is and how little the simulation holds up. The game does not survive comparison to GTA or RDR in this regard. Try following an NPC after a quest sometime. Try remaining somewhere a bit longer than the pre-programmed dialogue betweens NPCs.

I assume story is the saving grace.. as expected from reds so I'm gonna stick with it but I'm rather diappointed since I expected much more from this game, especially considering the review score it has.

negative.original:
This is a highly overrated game, essentially sci-fi GTA but worse.

I bought this game because I read reviews and comments that described it as an open world RPG; some people commented that it is "like a science fiction Skyrim." I spent 4 hours creating my character and going through the tutorial stage; after I got into the world and saw this game for what it really is it was already too late to get a refund (denied twice). So I played it some more to give it a chance.

This game is NOT an RPG. You are a pre-determined character that is just walking through a pre-set story on rails with a few possible different game endings. In one case I rescued an annoying monk from a gang who was going to give him cyberware against his wishes. I killed the gang to rescue him, and then he insults me saying I am worse than the gang members because I killed them. I immediately tried to kill him for insulting me like that, but the game wouldn't let me! I don't think this character is tied to a later quest, the game just refused to let me kill him because the game wants to force its morality onto you. The game is constantly pushing its moral message at you, your contacts always whine about you killing criminals and scum. Some cyber-freak could kill 20 people and then I go deal with him and he attacks me and I kill him. Then, my contact cries about it and harangues me. If this was an RPG, then I would be able to kill that stupid monk and I would just do missions for a different contact that appreciated my abilities. But this is not an RPG - you don't create your own identity, you don't make a character or even pick a name. You have hit points, you get to pick your appearance and you get to pick skills from a skill tree - that is not what it means to be a role playing game.

The world is boring and repetitive. It's just a sprawling city of closed doors with nothing behind them (well, you can't even open most doors or buildings), except a few areas that are defined for the mission objectives.

translations.japanese:
This is a highly overrated game, essentially sci-fi GTA but worse.

I bought this game because I read reviews and comments that described it as an open world RPG; some people commented that it is "like a science fiction Skyrim." I spent 4 hours creating my character and going through the tutorial stage; after I got into the world and saw this game for what it really is it was already too late to get a refund (denied twice). So I played it some more to give it a chance.

This game is NOT an RPG. You are a pre-determined character that is just walking through a pre-set story on rails with a few possible different game endings. In one case I rescued an annoying monk from a gang who was going to give him cyberware against his wishes. I killed the gang to rescue him, and then he insults me saying I am worse than the gang members because I killed them. I immediately tried to kill him for insulting me like that, but the game wouldn't let me! I don't think this character is tied to a later quest, the game just refused to let me kill him because the game wants to force its morality onto you. The game is constantly pushing its moral message at you, your contacts always whine about you killing criminals and scum. Some cyber-freak could kill 20 people and then I go deal with him and he attacks me and I kill him. Then, my contact cries about it and harangues me. If this was an RPG, then I would be able to kill that stupid monk and I would just do missions for a different contact that appreciated my abilities. But this is not an RPG - you don't create your own identity, you don't make a character or even pick a name. You have hit points, you get to pick your appearance and you get to pick skills from a skill tree - that is not what it means to be a role playing game.

The world is boring and repetitive. It's just a sprawling city of closed doors with nothing behind them (well, you can't even open most doors or buildings), except a few areas that are defined for the mission objectives.

i have mixed feeling when i played cyberpunk, the lore and world building is phenomnal , it reminded me how much i miss Deux ex series, however the gameplay approach and the quest design is honestly quite terrible it learned all the wrong lessons from GTA series and it dose not help the fact driving in this game is not fun and the road is not big enough to drive around.
the gunplay is fund and the game is teahcnically stable but i had some major technical problems with the phantom liberty DLC despite having new specs.

If cyberpunk took the sand-box approach with more focus on the quest design it could have been better game instead CDPR decided to chase after the GTA market share which resulted in major flaws of the game

It's possible that the game would eventually pick up its pace and get better, but I'm not paying to see.

A 30$ DLC should've been a nail in a coffin for this game after all it's BS.

negative.original: 很一般的游戏，看似开放世界其实线性的要死，剧情短的像蛆，经济系统和商店跟摆设没区别，游戏里的服装几乎也都很丑，既不赛博也不朋克，全是五颜六色的束脚裤运动鞋幽默穿搭，不知道的还以为是和平精英里跑出来的。原作桌游的背景故事设定比游戏有趣100倍，这么宏大和深刻的世界观可惜被波兰蠢驴做成了罐头，营销号和b站抖音笔电男大口中的神作，不如曾经的巫师3一根

negative.original:
It's like CyberPunk themed Grand Theft Auto with far better graphics and more in-depth plot and play.

However, do you enjoy having to click through literal hours of dialogue and cut scenes, which you often can't skip, and have to sit there and click to progress..? I don't.

For that reason, and many other tedious and poor developer choices, it makes it incredibly difficult to enjoy the game.

Also, it says I've only played like an hour, but it's probably closer to 40 hours.

I've gotten to the point where I don't care what the plot is, because I don't have an hour to click through every mini-movie cutscene. I literally button-mash to make it go as fast as possible during the few times it let's you fast-forward a few lines at a time.

Yes, I'm still playing it, but I rarely play main-plot missions, which make me very impatient and bored.

negative.original:
This is a weird one.  As proved by the hours played, I've finished the game along with the Phantom Liberty DLC, but have no desire to play it again.  

First, the pros:

Gameplay and voice acting is good, and I experienced no issues with the performance.  Many of the systems are enjoyable, especially the driving, combat, and hacking, and there truly are many ways to play this game.  I had some issues of taste with some crafting system in that it feels pretty shallow and the weapons you can make are not as interesting or powerful as the drops.

Now, the reason for my negative review: the theme and setting.

This game's setting is absolutely disgusting.  I fully understand that this is supposed to be social commentary on the nihilism, greed, consumerism, lasciviousness and techno-obsession of the modern world, but the experience of playing through all that left me feeling gross.  I kept waiting for some kind of heart in the game that would make me care more about the characters, and while the main conflict V ultimately faces is (kind of) interesting, and the choices you have to make do have impact, it still all against this backdrop of hopelessness, moral relativism, and grime that feels so depressing.

If you enjoy that sort of experience, go ahead and play this.  The game is well designed and does what it tries to do quite well.  I just won't recommend the feeling.

I felt similarly about What Remains of Edith Finch, another modern, highly rated game whose story left me feeling as if I'd just spent way too long in a modern art museum looking at, at best, some screwed up interpretation of beauty, and at worst, an intentional display of ugliness.

I fully understand that this is supposed to be social commentary on the nihilism, greed, consumerism, lasciviousness and techno-obsession of the modern world, but the experience of playing through all that left me feeling gross.  I kept waiting for some kind of heart in the game that would make me care more about the characters, and while the main conflict V ultimately faces is (kind of) interesting, and the choices you have to make do have impact, it still all against this backdrop of hopelessness, moral relativism, and grime that feels so depressing.

If you enjoy that sort of experience, go ahead and play this.  The game is well designed and does what it tries to do quite well.  I just won't recommend the feeling.

I felt similarly about What Remains of Edith Finch, another modern, highly rated game whose story left me feeling as if I'd just spent way too long in a modern art museum looking at, at best, some screwed up interpretation of beauty, and at worst, an intentional display of ugliness.

negative.original:
I want to like this game. I like the premise, the city is inviting exploration.
But as soon as you divert from the main storyline, the whole illusion collapses like a house of cards.

Nope, you are not a Night City resident. Just the hero of a rushed videogame. Everything is way to gamified, the world revolves around you, everyone wants to talk to you and you get the best ♥♥♥♥ practically gifted. An extremely casual open-world experience with only a thin shell of immersion.

I'm not expecting a hard-core simulation experience, but this open-world title actively breaks immersion and thus fails to be convincing outside of the linear main story gameplay - and even there it's interrupted by occasional glitches.

I really hope the next title will receive more attention to deep immersion in the open world and much more polish than this one.

Dont waste your time unless you have a god PC. I have a decent setup and can/could never get this game to run at anything more than 25fps. No matter how many chances I give this slop game, It shows me why I dont like it. Even if I sit through the terrible experience of having low frames, It's still not a good game. Combat is ok, driving is terrible... the city is practically dead because you wont be able to run the game without removing 95% of the population... 

3/10 game, mainly due to optimization.

negative.original: We are in 2026, 5years after launch and binding keys is still a headache apparently !!! I play on a french AZERTY keyboard, I've paid to play on PC, not on PC+controller. Despite good reviews I do not want to risk having to deal with bad UI & gameplay or take wrong decision simply because it is "QWERTY" in menu. I can solve this using mod or changing inputUserMappings.xml by myself but they have already wasted 2h of my time. Life is too short, so why spending it making the work of lazy people (or greedy seing the game launch mess). I sincerly hope they will manage to correct this bad trajectory on Witcher 4.
